Detailed Correspondence
Notice of Pre-AIA  or AIA  Status
The present application, filed on or after March 16, 2013, is being examined under the first inventor to file provisions of the AIA .
Information Disclosure Statement
The information disclosure statement filed 02/14/2023 fails to comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.97, 1.98 and MPEP § 609 because no English translation of Notice of Allowance from Korean Application dated January 13, 2022 is provided.  It has been placed in the application file, but the information referred to therein has not been considered as to the merits.  Applicant is advised that the date of any re-submission of any item of information contained in this information disclosure statement or the submission of any missing element(s) will be the date of submission for purposes of determining compliance with the requirements based on the time of filing the statement, including all certification requirements for statements under 37 CFR 1.97(e).  See MPEP § 609.05(a).
Drawings
The drawings are objected to because reference number “100” are shows twice pointing to different parts (Fig. 1, left hand side, the lower one should be “210).  Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment of the application. Any amended replacement drawing sheet should include all of the figures appearing on the immediate prior version of the sheet, even if only one figure is being amended. The figure or figure number of an amended drawing should not be labeled as “amended.” If a drawing figure is to be canceled, the appropriate figure must be removed from the replacement sheet, and where necessary, the remaining figures must be renumbered and appropriate changes made to the brief description of the several views of the drawings for consistency. Additional replacement sheets may be necessary to show the renumbering of the remaining figures. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date of an application must be labeled in the top margin as either “Replacement Sheet” or “New Sheet” pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). If the changes are not accepted by the examiner, the applicant will be notified and informed of any required corrective action in the next Office action. The objection to the drawings will not be held in abeyance.
Specification
The disclosure is objected to because of the following informalities: “The dielectric plate 200” at the top of page 10 should be “The dielectric plate 220” .
Appropriate correction is required.
Claim Interpretations
The “a support plate on which a substrate is placed’ of claim 1, Applicants’ Fig. 2 shows the substrate W is above the support plate 210 and indirectly supported by the support plate 210 (directly supported by pin 1100) and will be examined accordingly.
Claim 16 recites “wherein the first plate includes a dielectric substance, and the second plate includes an insulating substance”, it is note that a dielectric substance is an insulating substance. Any minute difference in the first plate and the second plate is considered read into the claim.
It is also well-known that the bending of thermal expansion is between two adjacent layer that are connecting to each other (see also Applicants’ Fig. 8, bending due to thermal expansion difference between the dielectric plate 220 and the lower plate 230). As the lower plate 230 being a conductive material (with cooling channels), having a much larger thermal expansion difference than the dielectric/insulating substance. The examiner notices that the lower plate 230 and the dielectric plate 220 are lumped into the support plate 210 in claim 1. In claims 9-16, the lower plate is never mentioned. Therefore, it can be considered as either part of the dielectric plate 220 or part of the insulating plate 250.
The following limitations are considered a determination process for making the apparatus:
The “wherein a volume of each of the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the support plate and the insulating plate” of claim 5,
the “wherein the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the support plate and the insulating plate“ of claim 6,
the “wherein a volume of each of the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first plate and the second plate” of claim 13,
the “wherein the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first plate and the second plate” of claim 14,
the “wherein the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the dielectric plate, the lower plate. and the insulating plate” of claim 20,
the determination/decision before making the apparatus is not part of the structure of the apparatus.
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 112
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112(b):
(b)  CONCLUSION.—The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph:
The specification shall conclude with one or more claims particularly pointing out and distinctly claiming the subject matter which the applicant regards as his invention.
Claims 9-16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA ), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA  35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention.
Claim 9 recites “the support plate” in line 10, there is no antecedent basis for this term.
Claim 9 will be examined inclusive “the first plate” instead of “the support plate”
Claim 12 is rejected as it depends on itself.
Claim 15 recites “wherein the amount of thermal deformation of the plate is larger than the amount of thermal deformation of the second plate”, this raises an antecedent issue.
Furthermore, Applicants dielectric plate 220 seems to be the claimed first plate while the lower plate 230 seems to be the second plate. The lower plate 230 is a thermal conductor typical has larger thermal expansion than the dielectric first plate 220. The examiner cannot find exactly what material the lower plate 230 is and which conductor having a smaller thermal expansion than the dielectric plate 220.
Claim will be examined inclusive any plate in the support unit being compared to the second plate.
Dependent claims 10-16 are also rejected under USC 112(b) at least due to dependency to rejected claim 9.
Claim Rejections - 35 USC § 103
The following is a quotation of 35 U.S.C. 103 which forms the basis for all obviousness rejections set forth in this Office action:
A patent for a claimed invention may not be obtained, notwithstanding that the claimed invention is not identically disclosed as set forth in section 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.
The factual inquiries for establishing a background for determining obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 are summarized as follows:
1. Determining the scope and contents of the prior art.
2. Ascertaining the differences between the prior art and the claims at issue.
3. Resolving the level of ordinary skill in the pertinent art.
4. Considering objective evidence present in the application indicating obviousness or nonobviousness.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Hara et al. (JP H06333810, from IDS, hereafter ‘810), in view of Matyushkin et al. (US 20080017104, hereafter ‘104). (US 20110292562 is evidenced for ESC deformation due to thermal expansion difference).
‘810 teaches some limitations of:
Claim 1: A drop out preventing member 18 is incorporated in a substrate mounting stand 4 along a hole 10 provided to the substrate mounting stand 4 (abstract, includes the claimed “A support unit for supporting a substrate, the support unit comprising: a support plate on which a substrate is placed”);
a metal substrate mounting table 4 is arranged on the upper surface of the surface heating heater 2, and a heater pressing plate 6 is arranged on the lower surface thereof (middle of page 2, description applicable to the invention of ‘810, includes the claimed “a heater provided inside the support plate and configured to heat the substrate”);
the retaining member 18 made of bimetal in which two materials 28 and 30 having different thermal expansion coefficients are bonded to each other is attached to the built-in space 24 provided in the substrate mounting table 4 (middle of page 5), the retaining member is deformed as the temperature rises and extends downward from the head (middle of page 3, above [0015], includes the claimed “and a bimetal member disposed inside the support plate and configured to compensate for bending of the support plate due to heat”),
the proximity pins 12 functioning as substrate supporting members for supporting the substrate W in the holes 10 are respectively detachable (middle of page 2, includes the claimed “wherein the bimetal member includes: a pin provided to be in contactable with a bottom surface of the substrate that is placed on the support plate”; the two metal materials 28 and 30 is the claimed “a first member configured to support the pin; and a second member provided to surround the first member”),
at a high temperature, as shown in FIG. 8, when a part of the retaining member 18 is adjusted so as to contact the body portion 16 of the proximity pin 12 so as to tighten the proximity pin 12, the retaining member 18 causes the proxy to move (lower portion of page 5, includes the claimed “and the pin is provided to move up or move down according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member”, as the temperature continue to rise, the thermal expansion difference is capable of moving the proximity pin 12 up and down).
‘810 does not teach the other limitations of:
Claim 1: (a support plate on which a substrate is placed), and which includes an electrostatic electrode providing electrostatic force to the substrate.
an insulating plate provided under the support plate as an insulating substance.
‘810 is silent on the wafer chucking mechanism and the material of the pressing plate 6.
‘104 is an analogous art in the field of SUBSTRATE PROCESSING WITH RAPID TEMPERATURE GRADIENT CONTROL (title), A substrate processing chamber comprises an electrostatic chuck comprising a ceramic puck having a substrate receiving surface and an opposing backside surface (abstract), including lift pins ([0052]). ‘104 teaches that The substrate 25 is held in the chamber 106 on a receiving surface 26 of a substrate support comprising an electrostatic chuck 20 which in turn rests on a base 91. The electrostatic chuck 20 comprises a ceramic puck 24 having a substrate receiving surface 26 which is the top surface of the puck 24, and serves to hold a substrate 25, as shown in FIGS. 1 and 2 ([0020]), The electrode 36 embedded in the ceramic puck 24 is used to generate an electrostatic force to retain a substrate placed on the substrate receiving surface 26 ([0022]), The base 91 comprises a metal body 92 ([0032], 2nd sentence, notice that the ceramic puck 24 and metal body 92 interface has a mismatch in thermal expansion). Note also the unlabeled layer between the metal body and the grounded chamber has to be an insulator to prevent short circuit as various power lines for electrode and heater passing through this layer.
Before the effective filing dates of the claimed invention, it would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art to have adopted an electrostatic chuck with an insulation plate in Fig. 1 of ‘104 as the mounting table 4 of ‘810, for its suitability for holding a substrate with predictable result. The selection of something based on its known suitability for its intended use has been held to support a prima facie case of obviousness. MPEP 2144.07. The combination is shown in illustration below.

‘810 also teaches some limitations of:
Claim 9: A drop out preventing member 18 is incorporated in a substrate mounting stand 4 along a hole 10 provided to the substrate mounting stand 4 (abstract, includes the claimed “A support unit for supporting a substrate, the support unit comprising: a first plate on which a substrate is placed”);
a metal substrate mounting table 4 is arranged on the upper surface of the surface heating heater 2, and a heater pressing plate 6 is arranged on the lower surface thereof (middle of page 2, description applicable to the invention of ‘810, includes the claimed “a heater provided inside the first plate to heat the substrate; a second plate provided under the first plate”);
the retaining member 18 made of bimetal in which two materials 28 and 30 having different thermal expansion coefficients are bonded to each other is attached to the built-in space 24 provided in the substrate mounting table 4 (middle of page 5), the retaining member is deformed as the temperature rises and extends downward from the head (middle of page 3, above [0015], includes the claimed “and a bimetal member disposed inside the first plate and configured to compensate for bending of the first plate”),
the proximity pins 12 functioning as substrate supporting members for supporting the substrate W in the holes 10 are respectively detachable (middle of page 2, includes the claimed “wherein the bimetal member includes: a pin provided to be in contactable with a bottom surface of the substrate that is placed on the support plate”); the two metal materials 28 and 30 is the claimed “a first member configured to support the pin; and a second member provided to surround the first member”),
at a high temperature, as shown in FIG. 8, when a part of the retaining member 18 is adjusted so as to contact the body portion 16 of the proximity pin 12 so as to tighten the proximity pin 12, the retaining member 18 causes the proxy to move (lower portion of page 5, includes the claimed “and the pin is provided to move up or move down according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member”, as the temperature continue to rise, the thermal expansion difference is capable of moving the proximity pin 12 up and down).
‘810 does not teach the other limitations of:
Claim 9: a second plate provided under the first plate in a different material from a material of the first plate.
‘104 teaches the base 91 comprises a metal body 92 ([0032], 2nd sentence) as discussed above.
Before the effective filing dates of the claimed invention, it would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art to have adopted an electrostatic chuck in Fig. 1 of ‘104 that has a metal body 92 below the ceramic puck 24 as the mounting table 4 of ‘810, for its suitability for holding a substrate with predictable result. The selection of something based on its known suitability for its intended use has been held to support a prima facie case of obviousness. MPEP 2144.07.
‘810 also teaches some limitations of:
Claim 17: The present invention relates to a heat treatment apparatus for heating a substrate such as a rectangular glass substrate for liquid crystal or a semiconductor wafer ([0001], includes the claimed “A substrate treating apparatus, comprising”):
a metal substrate mounting table 4 is arranged on the upper surface of the surface heating heater 2, and a heater pressing plate 6 is arranged on the lower surface thereof (middle of page 2, description applicable to the invention of ‘810, includes the claimed “a heater provided to heat the substrate”);
A drop out preventing member 18 is incorporated in a substrate mounting stand 4 along a hole 10 provided to the substrate mounting stand 4 (abstract), the retaining member 18 made of bimetal in which two materials 28 and 30 having different thermal expansion coefficients are bonded to each other is attached to the built-in space 24 provided in the substrate mounting table 4 (middle of page 5), the retaining member is deformed as the temperature rises and extends downward from the head (middle of page 3, above [0015], includes the claimed “a bimetal member configured to compensate for bending of the dielectric plate due to heat”),
the proximity pins 12 functioning as substrate supporting members for supporting the substrate W in the holes 10 are respectively detachable (middle of page 2, includes the claimed “wherein the bimetal member includes: a pin provided to be in contactable with a bottom surface of the substrate”; the two metal materials 28 and 30 is the claimed “a first member configured to support the pin; and a second member provided to surround the first member”),
at a high temperature, as shown in FIG. 8, when a part of the retaining member 18 is adjusted so as to contact the body portion 16 of the proximity pin 12 so as to tighten the proximity pin 12, the retaining member 18 causes the proxy to move (lower portion of page 5, includes the claimed “and the pin is provided to move up or move down according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member”, as the temperature continue to rise, the thermal expansion difference is capable of moving the proximity pin 12 up and down).
‘810 does not teach the other limitations of:
Claim 17: a dielectric plate on which a substrate is placed, and which includes an electrostatic electrode therein and is provided as a dielectric substance;
a lower plate disposed under the dielectric plate and provided with a cooling flow path therein;
(a heater provided inside) the dielectric plate (to heat the substrate);
an insulating plate provided under the lower plate as an insulating substance;
(a bimetal member disposed) inside the dielectric plate (and configured to compensate for bending of the dielectric plate due to heat),
(wherein the bimetal member includes: a pin provided to be contactable with a bottom surface of the substrate) that is placed on the dielectric plate;
‘104 is an analogous art as discussed above.
Before the effective filing dates of the claimed invention, it would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art to have adopted an electrostatic chuck in Fig. 1 of ‘104 as the mounting table 4 of ‘810, for its suitability for holding a substrate with predictable result. The selection of something based on its known suitability for its intended use has been held to support a prima facie case of obviousness. MPEP 2144.07.
‘810 further teaches the limitations of:
Claims 3 and 11: the retaining member 18 made of bimetal in which two materials 28 and 30 having different thermal expansion coefficients are bonded to each other is attached to the built-in space 24 provided in the substrate mounting table 4 (middle of page 5, includes the claimed “wherein a thermal deformation rate of the first member is different from a thermal deformation rate of the second member”).
Claims 4, 12, and 19: The retaining member 18 is made of a material having a coefficient of thermal expansion higher than that of the material of the substrate mounting table 4 (3rd complete paragraph of page 4, a supporting evidence), at a high temperature, as shown in FIG. 8, when a part of the retaining member 18 is adjusted so as to contact the body portion 16 of the proximity pin 12 so as to tighten the proximity pin 12, the retaining member 18 causes the proxy to move (lower portion of page 5, therefore, the material 30 has to have a higher thermal expansion to tighten the proximity pin, includes the claimed “wherein the thermal deformation rate of the first member is larger than the thermal deformation rate of the second member”).
Claims 5-6, 13-14, and 20: the determination process is not part of the apparatus, see claim interpretation above (the claimed “wherein a volume of each of the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the support plate and the insulating plate” of claims 5/13 and “wherein the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the support plate and the insulating plate” of claims 6/14 and “wherein the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the dielectric plate, the lower plate. and the insulating plate” of claim 20). Furthermore, claims 5-6 do not include the specific relationship between the relationship between the volume of the two members and the difference in thermal deformation between the support plate and the insulating plate. A determination that no relationship between these two quantities is also a determination.
Claim 7: In the above embodiment, one retaining member 18 is arranged in each hole 10 to prevent the proximity pin 12 from coming out of the hole 10. As shown, one retaining member 18 may be arranged for every three holes 10 (bottom of page 5, before [0029], includes the claimed “wherein a plurality of bimetal members is provided, and each of the bimetal members is disposed in a hollow hole formed inside the support plate”).
The combination of ‘810 and ‘104 teaches the limitations of:
Claims 2, 10, and 18: As shown in the illustration above, Fig. 1 of ‘104 having the dielectric- metal-insulating structure same as Applicants’ FIG. 2, along with the thermal expansion relationship discussed in claim 4 above, the combination would have the property of “wherein a movement direction of the pin according to the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is a direction opposite to a direction in which the support plate is bent according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the support plate and the insulating plate in a region in which the bimetal member is provided” of claims 2 and 10 and “wherein the difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the first member and the second member is determined according to a difference in the amount of thermal deformation between the dielectric plate, the lower plate. and the insulating plate” of claim 20.
Claim 8: The electrostatic chuck 20 comprises a ceramic puck 24 having a substrate receiving surface 26 which is the top surface of the puck 24, and serves to hold a substrate 25, as shown in FIGS. 1 and 2 (‘104, [0020]), The electrode 36 embedded in the ceramic puck 24 is used to generate an electrostatic force to retain a substrate placed on the substrate receiving surface 26, and optionally, to capacitively couple energy to the plasma formed in the chamber 106 ([0022], includes the claimed “wherein the support plate includes: a dielectric plate on which the substrate is placed, and which includes the electrostatic electrode therein and is provided as a dielectric substance”);
The base 91 has a coolant channel 110 ([0033], includes the claimed “and a lower plate disposed under the dielectric plate and provided with a cooling flow path therein”),
In the above embodiment, one retaining member 18 is arranged in each hole 10 to prevent the proximity pin 12 from coming out of the hole 10. As shown, one retaining member 18 may be arranged for every three holes 10, (‘810, bottom of page 5, before [0029], in the combination, the holes has to be in the imported ceramic puck 24 from ‘104, includes the claimed “and the bimetal member is disposed in the hollow hole formed inside the dielectric plate”).
Claim 15: by considering the base 91 and the ceramic puck 24 as the “plate”, it reads into the claimed “wherein the amount of thermal deformation of the plate is larger than the amount of thermal deformation of the second plate”.
Claim 16: the illustration above also shows that “wherein the first plate includes a dielectric substance, and the second plate includes an insulating substance”.
In case Applicants argue that ‘104 only teaches thermal expansion stresses that cause cracking ([0038]) but does not teach bending or deformation in regarding to claims 2, 10, and 18, and 5-6, 13-14, and 20. US 20110292562 is cited thermal expansion mismatch resulting bending or deformation (Figs. 3A-3B, [0004]).
Conclusion
The prior art made of record and not relied upon is considered pertinent to applicant's disclosure. US 5914568 is cited for distortion due to thermal stress (Fig. 1, col. 1, lines 40-42).
